title: Offset origin of DNS compression pointer
summary: When the two high-order bits in the name are 11, the low-order 14 bits of the two-byte entry give the offset from the first byte of the DNS message.
detail: A sequence can start with a normal label and end with a pointer. The pointer replaces the remaining suffix, consuming two bytes at the current position.
boundary: The two-byte message length attached to the TCP transfer does not belong to the DNS message body and cannot be counted in the offset.
relevance: When manually reviewing duplicate domain names in captured packets, avoid calculating offsets from the current record.
